title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with new partnerships and funding rounds as companies scramble to enhance their capabilities. Meanwhile, budget allocations are on the rise, but not without their share of delays in hypersonic testing.

themes.title: Partnerships for LEO Expansion
themes.body: Eutelsat and Station Satcom's agreement to scale LEO services signals a growing interest in maritime connectivity. This move could set the stage for more collaborations as the demand for satellite services continues to rise.

themes.title: Funding for Innovative Ventures
themes.body: China’s Nayuta Space has successfully raised fresh funding for its aerodynamic-recovery rocket, showcasing the ongoing investment in next-gen space technologies. Similarly, True Anomaly's $190M Series C indicates that investors are keen on companies that can deliver tangible advancements.

themes.title: Budget Increases Amid Delays
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds $1.4B to space resilience, reflecting a strong commitment to bolstering national security in space. However, ongoing delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests highlight the challenges that still loom over ambitious defense projects.

themes.title: A New Era for Defense-Tech
themes.body: The defense-tech IPO window is showing signs of life, with companies like Palantir securing substantial extensions on contracts. This resurgence may lead to a wave of new entrants in the market, eager to capitalize on the growing intersection of AI and defense.
